title: Choosing a project and planning it

visuals.title: Match the project idea to the concepts it practises

stages.name: 1. Pick a small idea
stages.detail: Choose something you can finish. A small project that works beats a big one that crashes.

stages.name: 2. Write the features
stages.detail: List 3 to 5 things the user can do: add, show, search, save. These become your menu options.

stages.name: 3. Choose the data
stages.detail: Decide the struct (one record) and the array that holds many records.

stages.name: 4. One function per feature
stages.detail: Each menu option calls one function. main stays short.

stages.name: 5. Test and add file save/load
stages.detail: Get it working with the keyboard first, then add the file, then test wrong input.

goal: After this you can pick a project idea that fits the course, say which concepts it uses, keep its scope small, and break it into a menu, a struct, functions and a file.
warmup: Before a cricket match the team does not start by buying a trophy. First they choose the team, then decide who bats and who bowls, then they play. A project is the same. Choose a small idea you can finish, split the work into small jobs, and give each job to one function. The project is worth 15% of the grade, so planning early pays off.
definition: A good PF project uses as many course concepts as possible: menus (loops and switch), arrays or structures, functions, file handling, and clean input validation. Scope means how big the project is. Controlling scope means keeping the project small enough that you can finish it, test it and explain every line. Breaking down means splitting the project into pieces: one struct for one record, one function for each menu feature, and one file for saving data.
howItWorks: Start from the idea table. Each idea mixes the same course concepts in a different story. Pick the one you find interesting, because you will explain it in front of the class. Next, write the feature list in plain words: for a Library, that is add a book, show all books, search by title, issue a book, return a book, save and load. Each feature becomes one case in a menu and one function. The data becomes a struct (for example Book) and an array of that struct. Finally add a file so the data stays after the program closes. How to control scope: finish a small working version first (menu with add and show only), then add one feature at a time and test after each. Do not start with ten features. Teams should make sure that each member can explain any part. How to break into files: a single .cpp file is enough for this course, but keep the order tidy: includes, struct, constants, function prototypes, main, then the function definitions.

worked.problem: Write the smallest menu-driven program that could become the front of any project: show a menu, print a hello line for option 1, print Invalid choice for a wrong number, and stop on option 2.
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[/"Show menu"/]
  B --> C[/"Read choice"/]
  C --> D{"choice?"}
  D -->|1| E[/"Print hello"/]
  D -->|2| F[/"Print Bye"/]
  D -->|other| G[/"Print Invalid choice"/]
  E --> H{"choice is 2?"}
  G --> H
  F --> H
  H -->|No| B
  H -->|Yes| I([End])

sample.title: The smallest menu program: loop + switch
sample.expectedOutput:
1. Say hello
2. Quit
Choice: Hello from my project!
1. Say hello
2. Quit
Choice: Invalid choice
1. Say hello
2. Quit
Choice: Bye!

explanation.text: One variable remembers the user's menu choice.
do-while: the menu is always shown at least once.
The prompt. Most projects print the menu inside the loop.
switch picks the action. Each feature of your project becomes one case.
Handles every wrong number, so the program never does something silly.
Keep looping until the user picks Quit.

steps.note: The program starts. choice has no value yet.
Round 1: print the first menu line.
Ask for the choice. No endl, so the cursor waits on the same line.
switch jumps to case 1. It prints the hello line and break leaves the switch.
choice is 1, not 2, so the loop goes round again.
Round 2: the menu is printed again.
The user types 7, which is not a menu option.
No case matches, so default runs. A good menu always handles wrong choices.
7 is not 2, so the loop repeats.
Round 3: the menu is printed once more.
choice is 2, so the condition is false and the loop ends.

worked.problem: For the Student Result Management System, define a struct for one student (id, name, marks), create one record and print it with a Pass or Fail line.
pseudocode: IF marks >= 50 THEN PRINT Pass ELSE PRINT Fail
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B["Make Student s: 101, Ayesha, 88.5"]
  B --> C[/"Print id, name, marks"/]
  C --> D{"marks >= 50?"}
  D -->|Yes| E[/"Print Pass"/]
  D -->|No| F[/"Print Fail"/]
  E --> G([End])
  F --> G

sample.title: One record: a struct for a Student Result System
sample.expectedOutput:
ID: 101
Name: Ayesha
Marks: 88.5
Result: Pass

explanation.text: A struct groups the facts about ONE student in a single variable. This is the heart of the Result System and Library ideas.
Three members: a number, a name and marks.
Create one record and fill it in order: id, name, marks.
The dot reaches one member of the record.
A rule of the project (pass or fail) is just an if on a member. Later you will keep many records in an array of structs.

worked.problem: For a Tic-Tac-Toe project, store the board in a 3 by 3 char array, write a function that prints it with separators, and a function that tells whether a given player has a complete row.
pseudocode: IF true THEN PRINT X wins on row 0
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B["Make 3x3 board"]
  B --> C[/"printBoard(board)"/]
  C --> D{"rowWins(board, 0, X)?"}
  D -->|Yes| E[/"Print X wins on row 0"/]
  D -->|No| F([End])
  E --> F

sample.title: Tic-Tac-Toe board: 2-D array and two small functions

explanation.text: One function for one job: drawing the board. The column size 3 must be written in the parameter.
Nested loops walk over every row and column of the 2-D array.
Draw the separators between cells but not after the last cell.
Win checking is another small function that returns true or false.
A row wins when all three cells hold the same player's mark.
The whole game state is just this 3 by 3 table. A dot means an empty cell.
main only calls the helpers. Short main, small functions: the style your project should have.

mistakes.wrong:
// Plan: 15 features, 4 screens, graphics, sound...
// Result: nothing works the night before the demo
mistakes.right:
// Plan: menu + add + show + search + save/load
// Finish this, test it, then add extras
mistakes.error: Not a compiler error. Too big a scope is the most common reason projects fail. Make a small version that works first.
It compiles, but nobody can read or explain it. Break the work into one function per feature.

mistakes.wrong:
// Three team members copy different code,
// nobody understands the other parts
mistakes.right: // Every member can explain any part of the code
mistakes.error: Not a compiler error. Instructors may ask any member to explain or change any part of the code, so everyone must understand all of it.
Passing board[3][3] is one element outside the array, not the board. Pass only the name: printBoard(board);

examTips: If asked what a project demonstrates, name the concepts: loops and switch for the menu, structs or arrays for the data, functions, files, validation.
For a Tic-Tac-Toe style question remember: 2-D array for the board, functions for printing and win checking.
Answer 'why a struct?' with: it keeps all facts about one record (id, name, marks) together.
A menu program is a do-while loop with a switch inside it. Write that skeleton first in any exam question about a menu.
The project is 15% of the grade (as given in the course notes).
romanSummary: Acha project woh hai jis mein zyada se zyada course concepts hon: menu (loop aur switch), array ya struct, functions, file aur input validation.
Idea chunein jo chhota ho aur aap use khatam kar saken. Pehle chhota working version banayein, phir ek ek feature barhayein.
Har menu option ke liye ek function banayein aur main ko chhota rakhein. Ek record ke liye struct aur bohat se records ke liye array use karein.
Project grade ka 15% hai, is liye pehle se plan karein. Har member ko poora code samajh aana chahiye.
